title: Zero Copy Federation vs Reverse ETL for Real-Time Segmentation

steps.prompt: Marketing needs Snowflake behavioral scores in Salesforce for near-real-time segmentation. The lake holds 50TB of raw clickstream; leadership rejects duplicating it into Salesforce storage or paying continuous API ingest fees. Which architecture best satisfies freshness, cost, and Trust?

options.label: Scheduled reverse ETL sync copying aggregated behavioral scores into Custom Big Objects via Bulk API
options.distractorAntipattern: Duplicating lake data into Big Objects incurs massive storage overhead, high ingest latency, and stale segmentation.
options.rationale: Copying massive telemetry into Custom Big Objects duplicates storage costs, creates pipeline lag, and violates leadership requirement to avoid data duplication.

options.label: Data 360 Zero Copy federation to Snowflake, querying governed lake shares directly without data movement
options.rationale: Zero Copy federation connects Data 360 directly to Snowflake shares, providing live query access for segmentation without data duplication or ingestion fees.

options.label: Synchronous External Services REST callouts querying Snowflake on-demand during segment evaluations
options.distractorAntipattern: Synchronous callouts during segmentation create severe API rate limiting, high latency, and lack lake-level SQL pushdown.
options.rationale: Synchronous API callouts cannot support complex audience segmentation queries across 50TB datasets and trigger severe API throttling.

title: DLO to DMO: Canonical Modeling Before Unification

steps.prompt: An ERP connector will land millions of party/order rows into Data 360. Architects must preserve source fidelity for reprocessing, expose a canonical Individual model for identity resolution, and later may replace a Contact DLO or install packaged Sales data kits. What modeling discipline is required?

options.label: Ingest into Data Lake Objects (DLO), map fields to standard Data Model Objects (DMO), and maintain verified primary key lineage
options.rationale: Staging data in DLOs preserves raw source fidelity, while mapping to standardized DMOs establishes the canonical layer required for identity resolution and modular stream replacement.

options.label: Ingest ERP streams directly into Unified Individual DMOs, bypassing intermediate Data Lake Objects to maximize ingest speed
options.distractorAntipattern: Ingesting directly into DMOs is technically impossible in Data 360 and destroys raw source auditability.
options.rationale: Data 360 architecture requires streams to land in DLOs first; bypassing DLO staging prevents raw data reprocessing and breaks platform lineage.

options.label: Unmap the active Contact DLO primary key from Individual before creating the new replacement stream to avoid mapping conflicts
options.distractorAntipattern: Unmapping primary keys from populated DMOs breaks downstream identity resolution rulesets and calculated insights.
options.rationale: Severing primary key mappings on active DMOs causes immediate failures across dependent identity resolution jobs and downstream calculated insights.

options.label: Deploy the packaged Sales Data Kit over existing custom DLO-to-DMO mappings to automatically standardize harmonized definitions
options.distractorAntipattern: Overwriting custom DLO-to-DMO mappings with default data kit templates silently breaks bespoke field mappings.
options.rationale: Deploying packaged data kits over customized DLO-DMO configurations overwrites custom relationships and breaks downstream segmentation and activation.

steps.prompt: A Data 360 Identity Resolution ruleset uses fuzzy match on Normalized Phone Number alone. Household members sharing a landline collapse into one Unified Individual, polluting consent and personalization. How should the architecture be revised?

options.label: Configure composite match criteria combining Phone with exact First Name or DOB, and preserve Unified Link DMOs for source lineage
options.rationale: Composite match rules prevent false-positive over-clustering across shared household identifiers, while Unified Link DMOs maintain full auditability to contributing source records.

options.label: Consolidate all source contact attributes directly onto the Unified Individual DMO and remove Unified Link objects to streamline joins
options.distractorAntipattern: Dropping Unified Link objects destroys record lineage and prevents downstream activations from tracing back to originating source keys.
options.rationale: Unified Link DMOs are architecturally required to maintain deterministic lineage between source records and unified profiles.

options.label: Update the profile reconciliation rule to Most Recently Updated while retaining the single-attribute fuzzy phone match criteria
options.distractorAntipattern: Reconciliation rules determine winning field values after clustering, but cannot correct erroneous cluster creation.
options.rationale: Reconciliation rules only decide which field value wins among already-matched profiles; they cannot unbundle incorrectly clustered individuals.

options.label: Replace Identity Resolution with a custom SQL Data Transform that hashes shared phone numbers into synthetic master person keys
options.distractorAntipattern: Custom key transforms bypass native graph unification, duplicate clustering logic, and do not update dynamically.
options.rationale: Manual SQL key transforms lack graph-based entity resolution, fail to handle multi-party cross-matching, and create unmaintainable custom pipeline debt.

title: Lakehouse Zero Copy: Iceberg Federation vs Bulk JDBC Copy

steps.prompt: A company keeps 100TB of telemetry in Databricks as Apache Iceberg tables (Parquet). Product wants Data 360 insights on that telemetry without paying to duplicate the lake into Salesforce storage. Which approach is Well-Architected?

options.label: Zero Copy federation via Iceberg REST Catalog metadata, querying Databricks Parquet tables in place
options.rationale: File-based Zero Copy queries Parquet/Iceberg data in place using open catalog metadata, avoiding storage duplication and compute double-billing.

options.label: Scheduled JDBC pipeline extracting 100TB into native Data 360 Data Lake Objects for local processing
options.distractorAntipattern: Extracting lakehouse data into Data 360 duplicates storage costs and introduces heavy batch ingestion latency.
options.rationale: Ingesting 100TB via JDBC duplicates storage, incurs massive credit consumption, and creates substantial data synchronization lag.

options.label: Micro-batch Ingestion API jobs streaming partitioned Parquet chunks into custom CRM staging tables
options.distractorAntipattern: Streaming big data telemetry into core CRM objects violates platform storage limits and triggers API throttling.
options.rationale: The Ingestion API is meant for lightweight JSON/CSV records, not multi-terabyte Parquet dumps, and staging in CRM objects exhausts database quotas.

title: Streaming vs Calculated Insights for Sub-Minute Triggers

steps.prompt: Commerce wants an engagement the moment a shopper views 3 products inside a 5-minute sliding window. Leadership will not accept next-day batch scores for this use case. Which Data 360 capability fits?

options.label: Streaming Insights with time-based sliding window aggregations over real-time event streams
options.rationale: Streaming Insights process real-time events continuously within sub-minute sliding time windows, triggering immediate downstream actions.

options.label: Calculated Insights configured with incremental hourly batch schedules on unified browse DMOs
options.distractorAntipattern: Calculated Insights run on multi-hour schedules and cannot evaluate sub-minute sliding session windows.
options.rationale: Calculated Insights are designed for periodic multidimensional batch aggregations, not real-time sub-minute event threshold evaluation.

options.label: Data Cloud Segment triggers refreshed continuously using rapid identity resolution updates
options.distractorAntipattern: Segment publishing is a periodic batch operation, not an event-driven stream processor.
options.rationale: Segment evaluation runs on schedules (typically every 12 to 24 hours) and cannot trigger real-time actions during active shopper browsing.

title: Data Actions: Bridging Insights to CRM Execution

steps.prompt: A Streaming Insight flags VIP churn risk above 85%. Retention must start in core CRM within minutes — without a custom polling service. How should Data 360 invoke the downstream workflow?

options.label: Configure a Data Action targeting a Platform Event or Flow when the threshold condition fires
options.rationale: Data Actions trigger near-real-time events or Salesforce Flows directly from Streaming Insights without requiring external middleware or polling.

options.label: Schedule a frequent Apex Queueable job polling the Data Cloud SQL Query API for updated scores
options.distractorAntipattern: Polling Data Cloud Query API from Apex wastes API calls, adds latency, and risks rate-limit exceptions.
options.rationale: Continuous polling from Apex consumes API quotas, adds latency, and creates tight coupling instead of event-driven execution.

options.label: Publish segment memberships to an Amazon S3 target and trigger an external webhook to CRM
options.distractorAntipattern: S3 segment activation introduces file export latency and requires external orchestration middleware.
options.rationale: File-based cloud storage activation introduces significant batch egress latency and violates the requirement for direct, near-real-time CRM invocation.

title: Unstructured Grounding: Chunking Knowledge in Data 360

steps.prompt: An Agentforce service agent must be grounded on PDF manuals and related Account files via Data 360 unstructured / search capabilities. Retrieval quality is poor, some PDFs never chunk, and stakeholders also want near-real-time file answers. Which approach best balances semantic coherence, product limits, and freshness?

options.label: Use section-aware chunking (250–500 tokens) on text PDFs, and leverage direct Agent Actions for real-time CRM file retrieval
options.rationale: Chunking between 250–500 tokens preserves semantic coherence. Complex tables should be preprocessed, and real-time CRM files are best queried via direct Agent Actions rather than waiting on periodic search index rebuilds.

options.label: Embed each entire multi-page PDF as a single comprehensive vector to preserve cross-paragraph context across the document
options.distractorAntipattern: Monolithic document embeddings exceed token limits, dilute retrieval similarity, and cause severe hallucination.
options.rationale: Single-vector document embeddings dilute semantic relevance, exceed embedding model context windows, and prevent precise chunk retrieval.

options.label: Ingest table-dense PDF manuals directly into unstructured search and enable automated OCR layout recognition in Data Cloud
options.distractorAntipattern: Data Cloud unstructured chunking does not reliably parse complex multi-column tables or dense tabular data without structured preprocessing.
options.rationale: Complex tabular data cannot be reliably indexed by standard unstructured text chunkers, resulting in skipped chunks and corrupted answers.

options.label: Rely entirely on Data Cloud search index re-indexing to expose newly uploaded Account attachments to Agentforce instantly
options.distractorAntipattern: Data Cloud vector indexing operates asynchronously and cannot deliver instantaneous grounding on newly attached files.
options.rationale: Vector search index updates are asynchronous batch processes and cannot guarantee sub-minute freshness for newly created record attachments.

title: Segment Activation: Cloud Storage Egress at Audience Scale

steps.prompt: Marketing activates a 20-million-profile segment to Amazon S3 every morning for ad platforms. The design must avoid CRM API ceilings and keep egress operationally simple. Which activation pattern fits?

options.label: Data 360 Cloud Storage Activation Target exporting compressed Parquet files directly to S3
options.rationale: Cloud Storage activation targets push bulk compressed datasets (Parquet/CSV) directly to external buckets without touching CRM API limits or consuming transactional worker threads.

options.label: Bulk API 2.0 query job exporting segment member IDs to an intermediate on-premise staging server
options.distractorAntipattern: Querying 20M rows through core CRM APIs creates significant extraction lag and consumes daily API allocations.
options.rationale: Extracting 20 million profiles via CRM Bulk API incurs heavy export processing time, staging infrastructure overhead, and API quota consumption.

options.label: Apex Batch job querying Unified Individual DMOs and streaming records to Amazon S3 via REST
options.distractorAntipattern: Querying DMOs from Apex batch is subject to SOQL limits, callout timeouts, and transaction heap ceilings.
options.rationale: Apex batch jobs cannot stream 20 million profiles to external endpoints without encountering transaction limits, heap errors, and callout timeouts.

title: Data Subject Erasure Across Data 360 Lake and Unified Profiles

steps.prompt: A customer submits a GDPR Right to Erasure request. Records exist in source CRM, Data 360 DLOs, unified DMOs, and derived insights. What must the architect ensure for complete compliance?

options.label: Execute a Data Subject Rights Forget Me request in Data 360 coordinated with source deletion to purge all layers
options.rationale: Data Subject Rights (DSR) requests in Data 360 ensure that personal data is deleted or masked across DLOs, unified profiles, and downstream search indexes, in alignment with source system erasures.

options.label: Delete the source Contact in CRM and rely on standard Data Cloud connector incremental syncs to cascade deletes
options.distractorAntipattern: Standard Data Cloud connectors append change records or soft deletes; they do not automatically purge historical lake data.
options.rationale: Standard data stream connectors append change events or mark deleted records, but do not physically erase historical immutable lake objects or derived insights.

options.label: Run an automated Data Transform to overwrite PII attributes with null values in harmonized Data Model Objects (DMOs)
options.distractorAntipattern: Overwriting fields in DMOs leaves raw PII stored in staging Data Lake Objects and immutable storage partitions.
options.rationale: Modifying DMO records does not remove historical PII residing in underlying Data Lake Objects, audit logs, or vector search embeddings.

title: Credit Economics: Stop Streaming Static Catalog Feeds

steps.prompt: Data 360 credits are burning down early each month. An audit finds 50 streaming connectors on product catalog tables that change about once a week, while scarce credit headroom is needed for real-time behavioral streams. What refactor is required?

options.label: Transition slow-changing catalog data streams from continuous streaming to daily batch ingestion
options.rationale: Streaming connectors consume continuous compute credits for micro-batch polling; switching weekly/daily reference data to scheduled batch drastically reduces credit burn.

options.label: Increase the streaming buffer flush interval to 60 minutes while keeping continuous connectors
options.distractorAntipattern: Adjusting flush intervals does not eliminate the fixed infrastructure credit cost of 50 active streaming listener connections.
options.rationale: Increasing flush intervals reduces message write frequency but still maintains 50 continuous streaming compute workers, yielding minimal credit savings.

options.label: Consolidate all 50 product catalog tables into a single high-frequency Ingestion API endpoint
options.distractorAntipattern: Directing 50 tables through a continuous Ingestion API endpoint still incurs streaming ingestion credit tariffs.
options.rationale: Streaming static reference data via the Ingestion API still bills at continuous streaming rates rather than lower-cost batch processing tiers.

title: Sales Data Kit Deploy vs Preserving Custom DLO–DMO Maps

steps.prompt: A mature Data 360 org already has customized Contact and Account DLO–DMO mappings powering identity resolution and activation. Marketing now requires Marketing Cloud Next, which mandates the Sales Data Kit. Leadership will not accept losing bespoke field maps, but consent/messaging kit coverage is still required. Which approach best protects the harmonized DMO layer?

options.label: Execute the automated Deploy Data Streams wizard in Marketing Cloud Next setup to reconcile custom and standard mappings into unified templates
options.distractorAntipattern: Blind Packaged Kit Redeploy
options.rationale: The standard Deploy wizard forces default data kit mappings, overwriting customized relationships and breaking active identity resolution models.

options.label: Retain custom mappings on existing DLOs and configure downstream segment activations to query Data Lake Objects directly instead of DMOs
options.distractorAntipattern: Lake-Only Activation Bypass
options.rationale: Marketing Cloud Next and Data Cloud segmentation require canonical Data Model Objects (DMOs) and cannot build unified audiences directly on DLOs.

options.label: Ingest required data kit streams selectively, preserving bespoke DLO-to-DMO harmonizations while mapping only mandatory messaging attributes
options.rationale: Ingesting required data kit streams manually or selectively avoids blowing away existing custom DLO-DMO mappings, preserving identity resolution integrity while fulfilling MCN prerequisites.

title: Account Engagement Needs Activation Targets, Not Link Alone

steps.prompt: A Marketing Cloud Account Engagement team already linked Account Engagement in Data 360 Setup. They expect Data 360 segments to show up as usable audiences in Account Engagement with no further work. Segments remain invisible. What completes the path so those audiences become available downstream?

options.label: Enable automated audience synchronization in Account Engagement connector settings to ingest all active segments
options.distractorAntipattern: Connect-Only Audience Expectation
options.rationale: Connecting the orgs does not automatically synchronize segments; audience delivery requires an explicit Activation Target and Segment Activation configuration.

options.label: Configure an Account Engagement Activation Target, then create and schedule Segment Activations for the target audience
options.rationale: Data Cloud requires both an Activation Target (specifying Account Engagement as destination) and individual Segment Activations to push audience memberships downstream.

options.label: Create a Data Action triggered by segment membership changes that writes prospect IDs via Account Engagement REST API
options.distractorAntipattern: Manual CSV Audience Re-Import
options.rationale: Building custom REST API pipelines using Data Actions introduces unnecessary integration complexity and maintenance overhead when native Activation Targets provide out-of-the-box syncing.

title: Test Data Must Use the Connector That Owns the Stream

steps.prompt: An architect built a Direct Access data stream → DLO → DMO → Flow path into CRM but has no access to the upstream Direct Access source. They need a few test rows to validate the Flow. Which approach respects how Data 360 ingestion actually works?

options.label: Use the Ingestion API to POST sample payloads directly into the existing Direct Access Data Lake Object to trigger the pipeline
options.distractorAntipattern: Arbitrary DLO Inject Bypass
options.rationale: Data Lake Objects are strictly coupled to their originating connector type; the Ingestion API cannot inject records into a DLO owned by a Direct Access stream.

options.label: Stand up a temporary Cloud Storage or File Upload stream mapped to the same target DMO to validate downstream Flow logic safely
options.rationale: Because connector-owned DLOs cannot be injected across connectors, creating a secondary stream mapped to the same harmonized DMO validates downstream Flow logic without corrupting upstream sources.

options.label: Temporarily repoint the CRM Flow to read simulated fixture records from a custom object until live connector access is restored
options.distractorAntipattern: CRM Fixture Path Substitution
options.rationale: Testing against a CRM custom object bypasses Data Cloud DMO schemas, data types, and trigger mechanics, leaving the real integration untested.

title: B2B ABM Go-Live: Activation Membership Without SFMC Duplication

moves.dialogueText: "ABM is in two weeks. Buying committees mean one Contact on several Accounts. Mapping a real Account Contact relationship adds a day of harmonization we do not have—can we just project Contact onto Account Contact and keep moving?"

options.text: Map Account Contact 1:1 from Contact so modeling finishes today and activation planning can start tomorrow.
options.techDebtImpact: Saves ~1 day now, but collapses many-to-many Account–person roles. Later membership work cannot express “this Contact in this Account” without duplication.

options.text: Spend the modeling day: Account Contact as the account–person relationship (e.g. AccountContactRelation), related to Account and Individual/Contact.
options.techDebtImpact: Burns schedule on DMO harmonization, but leaves a Customer 360 relationship grain that activation can membership on later.

moves.dialogueText: "The junction DMO is still category Other. Flipping it to Profile means recreate-or-transform work and re-testing relationships—half a sprint—before it shows under Activation Membership. Ship Other and hope the UI lists related DMOs?"

options.text: Leave category Other and protect the sprint; Activation Membership should accept any DMO related to Account or Contact.
options.techDebtImpact: Keeps the calendar intact, but Other-category junctions never appear under Activation Membership—marketing will fall back to Contact grain.

options.text: Pay the recreate/transform cost: set the junction to Profile, re-relate Account and Contact, then expose it under Activation Membership.
options.techDebtImpact: Consumes schedule on category change and remap, but Profile is what Activation Membership filtering expects for relationship-grain export.

moves.dialogueText: "Dry run: one Contact on two Accounts → two Contact rows in the Shared DE. Re-segmenting on the junction and rewiring membership is another build day. Leadership says activate on Contact and let SFMC dedupe—do we take that shortcut?"

options.text: Keep membership on Contact/Individual and lean on SFMC subscriber keys / journey dedupe so we do not rebuild the activation.
options.techDebtImpact: Avoids a rebuild day, but person-grain membership multiplies Shared DE rows per related Account; journeys inherit the duplication.

options.text: Rebuild: segment on Profile junction rows, set Activation Membership to the junction, traverse attributes to Contact/Individual as needed.
options.techDebtImpact: Costs a rebuild cycle, but membership matches the B2B relationship grain so Account sharing stops exploding Contact rows.

moves.dialogueText: "Compliance wants every Contact Point Email in the DE. Max # of Attribute Values is stuck at 1. A fan-out transform plus new segment/activation is another multi-day track—can we just raise the attribute limit instead?"

options.text: Raise Max # of Attribute Values on Contact Point Email (or a file-based activation DMO) and keep the existing membership object.
options.techDebtImpact: Looks like a same-day config win, but native activation will not fan out multiple emails per Individual via that limit—secondary addresses never become addressable rows.

options.text: Schedule the transform track: fan-out DLO/DMO (one row per Individual–email), segment on it, activate with membership on that grain.
options.techDebtImpact: Burns multi-day scope on transform + re-activation, but payload can choose a contact identifier per email row for compliance.

moves.dialogueText: "Activation fails on colliding Id attribute names across Individual, Contact Point Email, and Redshift. Renaming the payload and re-validating the DE eats the last buffer day. Marketing wants the raw API names left alone for ‘traceability’—ship as-is?"

options.text: Leave API-style Id attributes unchanged so we do not spend the buffer day on preferred names and DE revalidation.
options.techDebtImpact: Protects the last calendar day, but colliding names break or silently reshape the Shared DE under refresh.

options.text: Spend the buffer: assign preferred activation names that disambiguate source/meaning, keep only the identifiers SFMC needs, re-run with a clean payload.
options.techDebtImpact: Uses remaining schedule on payload hygiene so the Marketing Cloud DE stays stable across incremental refreshes.

title: ETL storage hoarding to Zero-Copy: 4-stage Data Virtualization refactor

stages.scenario: An enterprise replicates 50 million legacy ERP billing and invoice line records into custom sObjects via hourly scheduled ETL batch pipelines. The org has exceeded its licensed Salesforce data storage by 140%, resulting in heavy monthly storage overage penalties. Furthermore, batch API jobs frequently fail during peak hours due to 24-hour API limit exhaustion, leaving sales reps with out-of-sync invoice records. What is the fundamental architectural antipattern?

options.text: The architecture commits 'ETL Data Hoarding': replicating cold, read-mostly reference data into transactional Salesforce storage instead of querying it at source on demand via Data Virtualization.
options.coachingFeedback: Correct! The Salesforce Data Virtualization guide emphasizes that high-volume, read-mostly operational data should not be physically replicated into transactional relational storage, which wastes storage credits and consumes API limits.

options.text: The custom sObject should be converted into Big Objects to completely eliminate all API usage.
options.coachingFeedback: Misconception: Ingesting data into Big Objects still requires API calls and Async SOQL for complex querying; it does not eliminate ETL pipeline maintenance.

options.text: Hourly ETL pipelines are required by Salesforce for any external system containing more than 1 million records.
options.coachingFeedback: False: Salesforce encourages Zero Copy patterns and Data Virtualization via Salesforce Connect and Data 360 to eliminate unnecessary ETL pipelines.

stages.scenario: To eliminate physical storage overhead while providing seamless real-time access to ERP invoices directly on Account page layouts, what target pattern does the Data Virtualization fundamentals guide recommend?

options.text: Deploy Salesforce Connect with External Objects mapped to the data source (OData or Snowflake), configuring Query Pushdown, Indirect Lookups to Account, and dual governance through Named/Per-User Principals.
options.coachingFeedback: Correct! According to the Data Virtualization guide, Salesforce Connect with External Objects leverages Query Pushdown to execute filtering at source, renders external data seamlessly in standard UI components, and consumes zero Salesforce relational storage.

options.text: Build a custom Lightning Web Component that executes synchronous Apex HTTP REST callouts to the ERP system on every page load.
options.coachingFeedback: Antipattern: Ad-hoc Apex callouts in UI components lack native declarative integration (reports, Flow lookups, list views), risk thread exhaustion, and fail to leverage platform query pushdown optimizations.

stages.scenario: How should the enterprise safely transition users from the legacy custom sObject to External Objects without disrupting daily sales operations?

options.text: Deploy External Objects side-by-side on a dedicated Lightning page tab for a pilot user group, validate source query latency and Indirect Lookup indexing, and then decommission the hourly ETL jobs followed by staged truncation of the legacy custom object records.
options.coachingFeedback: Correct! Well-Architected migration prescribes side-by-side pilot validation to verify source query pushdown responsiveness before shutting down ETL replication and reclaiming physical storage.

options.text: Immediately delete all 50 million custom object records with Bulk API Hard Delete before setting up the External Data Source.
options.coachingFeedback: Catastrophic risk: Deleting legacy data before external connectivity and lookups are validated creates severe business downtime if the external connection fails.

stages.scenario: What observability mechanism should be implemented to ensure the virtualized data layer maintains high availability and stays within external callout constraints?

options.text: Monitor External Data Callout metrics via Event Monitoring, track OData response times and HTTP 429/500 status codes, and set automated alerts on named credential authentication expiration.
options.coachingFeedback: Correct! Real-time telemetry on External Data Callouts ensures architects can monitor source query latencies, detect external rate limits, and proactively refresh credentials before user sessions fail.

options.text: Assume the external system is always healthy since External Objects do not consume standard SOQL query rows.
options.coachingFeedback: Antipattern: External systems can suffer outages, latency degradation, or credential rotations that break the virtualized UI if unmonitored.
